say.en: The blue whale lives in the sea and breathes air; the platypus is a mammal that lays eggs; the crocodile has a heart like ours. Today we sort out the four land-vertebrate classes. In this lesson: State the distinguishing features of amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.
Recall their heart chambers and body temperature.
Give examples of each class.

body.en: Amphibians live both in water and on land. Their skin is moist and without scales, a tympanum represents the ear, and the gut, urinary and reproductive tracts open into a common cloaca. They breathe by gills, lungs and skin, have a three-chambered heart, are cold-blooded and show external fertilisation. Examples: Bufo, Rana, Hyla, Salamandra, and the limbless Ichthyophis. Reptiles have dry, cornified skin with scales or scutes and no external ear opening. Their heart is usually three-chambered, but four-chambered in crocodiles. They are cold-blooded, with internal fertilisation. Examples: Chelone, Testudo, Calotes, Crocodilus, Hemidactylus, Naja, Bungarus, Vipera.
body.kn: ಉಭಯಜೀವಿಗಳ ಚರ್ಮ ತೇವ, ಹುರುಪೆರಹಿತ; ಮೂರು ಕೋಣೆಯ ಹೃದಯ; ಬಾಹ್ಯ ಫಲೀಕರಣ. ಇಕ್ತಿಯೋಫಿಸ್ ಕಾಲಿಲ್ಲದ ಉಭಯಜೀವಿ. ಸರೀಸೃಪಗಳಿಗೆ ಒಣ ಹುರುಪೆ ಚರ್ಮ; ಮೊಸಳೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ನಾಲ್ಕು ಕೋಣೆಯ ಹೃದಯ.

title.en: On the board: Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves and Mammalia

say.en: Compare the four classes of land vertebrates.
Amphibians: moist skin without scales, a three-chambered heart, cold-blooded.
Reptiles: dry scaly skin, three chambers except four in crocodiles, cold-blooded.
Birds: feathers, four chambers, warm-blooded.
Mammals: hair and milk glands, four chambers, warm-blooded.
Special cases: the platypus lays eggs, and bird bones are hollow.

explanation.en: Amphibians live on land and in water; reptiles creep or crawl and have scaly skin; birds have feathers, a beak and air-filled bones; mammals have mammary glands and hair. The platypus is a mammal even though it lays eggs.

say.en: Four classes of land vertebrates. Sort the animals and features.

body.en: Birds have feathers, a beak and forelimbs modified into wings; most can fly, but some like the ostrich cannot. The skin is dry with no glands except the oil gland at the base of the tail. Long bones are hollow with air cavities (pneumatic). The digestive tract has a crop and a gizzard. The heart is four-chambered, they are warm-blooded, and air sacs connected to the lungs supplement breathing. Examples: Corvus, Columba, Psittacula, Struthio, Pavo, Aptenodytes, Neophron.

body.en: Mammals have mammary glands that make milk for the young, hair on the skin, external ears (pinnae) and different types of teeth. The heart is four-chambered and they are warm-blooded. Most are viviparous; the platypus, Ornithorhynchus, lays eggs. Examples: Macropus (kangaroo), Pteropus (flying fox), Delphinus (dolphin), Balaenoptera (blue whale), Elephas, Equus, Panthera tigris.
body.kn: ಸಸ್ತನಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಹಾಲು ಗ್ರಂಥಿಗಳು, ಕೂದಲು, ಕಿವಿಹಾಲೆ, ವಿವಿಧ ಬಗೆಯ ಹಲ್ಲುಗಳು. ಬಹುತೇಕ ಮರಿ ಹಾಕುತ್ತವೆ; ಪ್ಲಾಟಿಪಸ್ ಮೊಟ್ಟೆ ಇಡುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: Classify each animal: (a) Ichthyophis, (b) Pteropus, (c) Hemidactylus, (d) Aptenodytes. Give one reason for each.

steps.en: (a) Ichthyophis: Amphibia; it is a limbless amphibian with moist skin.
(b) Pteropus: Mammalia; the flying fox has hair and feeds its young on milk.
(c) Hemidactylus: Reptilia; the wall lizard has dry, scaly skin. (d) Aptenodytes: Aves; the penguin has feathers and a beak.

homework.en: Write three examples each of amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals with their genus names.

narration.en: Recap. Amphibians: moist skin, cloaca, three-chambered heart. Reptiles: dry scaly skin; crocodiles have four chambers. Birds: feathers, pneumatic bones, crop and gizzard. Mammals: mammary glands and hair; the platypus lays eggs.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಉಭಯಜೀವಿ: ತೇವ ಚರ್ಮ, ಕ್ಲೋಯಕ, ಮೂರು ಕೋಣೆಯ ಹೃದಯ. ಸರೀಸೃಪ: ಒಣ ಹುರುಪೆ ಚರ್ಮ; ಮೊಸಳೆಗೆ ನಾಲ್ಕು ಕೋಣೆ. ಪಕ್ಷಿ: ಗರಿ, ಟೊಳ್ಳು ಮೂಳೆ, ಕ್ರಾಪ್ ಮತ್ತು ಗಿಜರ್ಡ್. ಸಸ್ತನಿ: ಹಾಲು ಗ್ರಂಥಿ, ಕೂದಲು; ಪ್ಲಾಟಿಪಸ್ ಮೊಟ್ಟೆ ಇಡುತ್ತದೆ.
